grammar.name: Structuring an argument
grammar.scope: thesis, antithesis, synthesis; argumentative connectors (innanzitutto, d'altra parte, in secondo luogo, ne deriva che, in conclusione); the Italian 'tema argomentativo'

chapters.a_plot: 100 days before the maturità: Emma's class celebrates the traditional 'cento giorni'. Emma must also decide: Milan, Bologna or Chicago?
chapters.b_plot: Ben's cookbook, 'Un americano in Via dei Tigli', gets a publisher. He has to write the final chapter.
chapters.arc: Season premiere: Emma's decision arc and Ben's book arc.

grammar.name: Analysing poetry and literary texts
grammar.scope: vocabulary of analysis (il verso, la strofa, la metafora, l'enjambement, il tono, l'io lirico); commenting on a text; comparing interpretations

chapters.a_plot: Emma studies poetry with Ornella, who knows *L'infinito* by heart, and with Franco, who knows only football chants.
chapters.b_plot: Tommaso writes music to a Montale poem for his conservatory audition. Emma helps. Something is back between them.

grammar.name: The historical present and narrative style
grammar.scope: historical present in history writing and oral narration; switching tenses for vividness; dates and periods

chapters.theme: 20th-century Italian history: the Republic, the economic boom
chapters.a_plot: Emma's history revision: Ornella, Franco and Lucia each tell a piece of 20th-century history they lived. It becomes a family oral history.
chapters.b_plot: Leo's school project on 2 June (Festa della Repubblica) interviews Ornella, who voted in 1946... almost.
chapters.runner: Ornella's age math: was she even born? (She was, barely.)

grammar.name: Oral presentations
grammar.scope: opening and structuring a talk; signposting (passo ora a, come accennato, vorrei soffermarmi su); handling questions; formal spoken register

chapters.a_plot: Emma prepares her oral exam presentation: 'Due case, una lingua' (two homes, one language). She rehearses to the whole family at dinner.
chapters.b_plot: Chiara presents her first big project for Studio Ferri: the new community centre in the saved park.

grammar.name: The subjunctive: complete review
grammar.scope: all four tenses and all triggers; fixed expressions (che io sappia, sia chiaro, costi quel che costi, cascasse il mondo); independent subjunctive (che venga pure!)

chapters.a_plot: Emma's exam anxiety peaks. Every adult has advice, and all of it is subjunctive.
chapters.b_plot: Daniel has his own exams (terza media) and a crisis of confidence in Italian. Ben tells him about S1.

grammar.name: Hypothetical sentences: complete review
grammar.scope: types I, II, III and mixed; se omitted in formal style (avessi saputo...); alternatives (in caso di, qualora, a meno che); spoken imperfetto forms recognised

chapters.a_plot: Emma asks every adult: 'What would you have done if you'd chosen differently?' Chiara, Ben, Franco, Lucia and Grace all answer.
chapters.b_plot: Matteo wonders what would have happened if he'd never bought the bar. Nadia tells him: they'd never have met.

grammar.name: Journalistic register
grammar.scope: headlines, lead paragraphs, quotation verbs, passive and impersonal forms, nominal style in feature articles; writing a short article

chapters.a_plot: An architecture magazine features 'the park that a neighbourhood saved', with an interview with Chiara. She fears it will misrepresent the street.
chapters.b_plot: Roberto is misquoted in the article and demands a formal correction, in his finest bureaucratic Italian.
chapters.runner: Ben is described in the article as 'il marito americano'. He is offended; he's 'di Borgoverde'.

grammar.name: Legal and bureaucratic register
grammar.scope: fixed formulas (ai sensi di, in merito a, il sottoscritto, si fa presente che, entro e non oltre); passive and impersonal forms; decoding official documents

chapters.a_plot: Ben's Italian citizenship application (through marriage) is finally approved. The decree, the documents, and the oath at the town hall.
chapters.b_plot: Roberto, now fluent in Ben-speak, explains the documents in plain Italian: a complete reversal of S1.
chapters.arc: TENTPOLE: Ben becomes an Italian citizen.

grammar.name: Technical and descriptive register
grammar.scope: describing processes and objects precisely (si procede a, viene inserito, è costituito da, serve a); impersonal and passive forms; precise verbs

chapters.theme: Technology, how things work, trams and machines
chapters.a_plot: Franco takes Leo and Daniel to the tram depot where he worked. He explains how a 1928 'Carrelli' tram works, in the most precise Italian anyone has heard him speak.
chapters.b_plot: Nadia explains to Matteo how the new coffee machine for the second bar works. He doesn't listen, and the machine explodes (a small explosion).

title.it: Un americano in Via dei Tigli
title.en: An American on Via dei Tigli

grammar.name: Reviews and book language
grammar.scope: writing and reading reviews; evaluative adjectives and adverbs; nuance in praise and criticism (non privo di, tutt'altro che, a tratti)

chapters.a_plot: The book launch at Bar Tigli: 'Un americano in Via dei Tigli', a cookbook-memoir. Every neighbour finds themselves in it, and not everyone is happy about it.
chapters.b_plot: Ornella writes Ben's first review for the local paper: 'Tutt'altro che perfetto. Perfetto così.'

grammar.name: Humour, irony and wordplay
grammar.scope: irony markers (figurati, come no, sì, certo...); understatement; wordplay and puns; tone and intonation in writing

chapters.a_plot: Ben performs at an open mic comedy night in Milan, about being American in Italy. The Italian jokes land; the American ones don't.
chapters.b_plot: Nadia's irony finally meets its match: baby Anna, now 3, has inherited it.
chapters.runner: Franco doesn't laugh at anything, then laughs at the wrong thing.

grammar.name: Verbal periphrases
grammar.scope: mettersi a, stare per, stare a + infinitive, finire per / col, andare + gerund (va migliorando), venire + gerund, continuare a, tornare a

chapters.a_plot: Leo, 12, has grown ten centimetres, his voice is changing, and he's started closing his door. Ben and Chiara notice their second child leaving childhood.
chapters.b_plot: Franco and Leo's walks, which were once Franco teaching Leo, have turned into Leo teaching Franco (his phone).

title.en: I Wanted to Ask You Whether It Would Be Possible

grammar.name: Diplomacy and softening
grammar.scope: attenuation (volevo chiederLe, mi permetterei di, forse sarebbe il caso di, non vorrei sembrare...); indirect requests; softening disagreement

chapters.a_plot: Emma decides: Politecnico di Milano (architecture) with an exchange semester in Chicago. Now she has to tell the family, diplomatically, since everyone wanted something else.
chapters.b_plot: Lucia diplomatically tries to get Franco to stop driving. It takes the whole episode.

grammar.name: Lexical precision and synonyms
grammar.scope: replacing generic verbs (dire, fare, mettere, avere, cosa) with precise ones; synonyms and their register; avoiding repetition in writing

chapters.a_plot: The publisher's editor wants to 'correct' Ben's book, making his Italian more precise and less him. Ben and the editor fight over every verb.
chapters.b_plot: Emma edits her essays using Ornella's red pen. Ornella is merciless.
chapters.runner: Franco reviews the editor's corrections and agrees with Ben on every one.

grammar.name: Expressive personal writing
grammar.scope: the personal letter and diary; mixing tenses for reflection; imagery and emotion vocabulary; addressing a future self

chapters.a_plot: Emma writes a letter to her future self, echoing Anna's letter to Chiara (S3E18). Chiara gives Emma Anna's letter to read.
chapters.b_plot: Ben writes the last chapter of his book: a letter to the Ben who arrived in S1.
chapters.arc: Two letters: full circle for Anna's legacy.

grammar.name: Nuanced emotional vocabulary
grammar.scope: shades of emotion (malinconia, nostalgia, sollievo, rimorso, rammarico, commozione); idioms (avere un nodo alla gola, avere il cuore in gola, toccare il cielo con un dito)

key_vocab: toccare il cielo con un dito
chapters.a_plot: Ornella announces she will move to Genoa to live with her niece after the summer. The street takes it very badly, then very well.
chapters.b_plot: Tommaso is accepted at the conservatory in Florence. Emma and Tommaso face distance.

grammar.name: Discourse markers in spoken Italian
grammar.scope: dunque, ecco, comunque, allora, cioè, diciamo, per così dire, tra l'altro, a proposito, del resto; managing conversation and changing topic

chapters.a_plot: Emma and Daniel launch a podcast, 'Via dei Tigli', interviewing the neighbours. Episode one is Ornella: 90 minutes, no editing possible.
chapters.b_plot: Matteo is a podcast guest and can't stop saying 'cioè'. Nadia counts: 147.
chapters.runner: The podcast is secretly the frame for the season's final episodes.

grammar.name: Understanding TV, film and news
grammar.scope: fast speech features, elisions and truncations (buon, gran, fin), news broadcast structure, film dialogue vs written Italian

chapters.a_plot: A national TV news feature on 'the neighbourhood that saved its park', two years later. The family watches it together and critiques everything.
chapters.b_plot: Ben watches a Fellini film without subtitles for the first time and understands (almost) everything.
chapters.runner: Franco is recognised on the street as 'the tram speech man'.

grammar.name: Idioms and proverbs: review and use
grammar.scope: using idioms naturally and appropriately; register of idioms; transforming idioms creatively; knowing when not to use them

chapters.a_plot: Franco's proverb book (S7E19) comes back from the printer: one bound copy per grandchild. Each reads the proverb he chose for them.
chapters.b_plot: Ben realises Franco included a proverb for him too, under 'nipoti', not 'generi' (sons-in-law).

grammar.name: Summarising and paraphrasing
grammar.scope: techniques for summary (identifying main ideas, nominalisation, reporting verbs); paraphrasing with synonyms and restructuring; exam writing under time pressure

chapters.a_plot: Mid-June: the maturità written exams. The episode follows Emma through the exam, and the whole family through the waiting.
chapters.b_plot: The Festa dei Tigli committee decides to postpone the festa until after the orals, 'for Emma'. Roberto's idea.

grammar.name: Defending a position orally
grammar.scope: responding to challenges (capisco il punto, ma...; mi permetta di precisare; non a caso; è vero che..., tuttavia); linking disciplines; staying composed

chapters.a_plot: Emma's oral exam: 'Due case, una lingua'. The commission challenges her; she answers with the story of her family, and of the street.
chapters.b_plot: The family waits outside the school. Franco has brought a folding chair and sandwiches for everyone.

grammar.name: Review: future and probability
grammar.scope: futuro anteriore for supposition, condizionale for hearsay, congiuntivo for doubt; all ways of expressing probability together

chapters.a_plot: Waiting for the results. Every family member supposes something different about Emma's mark.
chapters.b_plot: Ornella's last weeks on the street: she gives away her things, each with a story.

title.en: That's How You Say It, But

grammar.name: Standard norms vs real usage
grammar.scope: optional subjunctive in speech, lui/lei vs egli/ella, gli for loro, a me mi, che polivalente; knowing the norm and the reality; generational language

chapters.a_plot: A grammar war at Sunday lunch: Ornella (purist) vs Leo and Daniel (TikTok Italian), with Ben as referee, the man who learned both.
chapters.b_plot: Roberto writes a letter to the newspaper about 'the decline of the Italian language' and receives a reply from Emma.
chapters.runner: 'A me mi piace' — is it allowed?

grammar.name: Rhetoric and speech writing
grammar.scope: rhetorical devices (anaphora, tricolon, rhetorical questions, antithesis); rhythm; balancing formal and personal; writing for the ear

chapters.a_plot: The committee asks Ben to give the speech at the Festa dei Tigli. He writes it with help from Emma, Ornella, Roberto and Franco (who crosses out half of it).
chapters.b_plot: Emma's results arrive on the morning of the festa. She keeps them secret all day, for the speech.

grammar.name: Final review: A1 to B2
grammar.scope: Consolidation of the whole course; the finale mirrors S1E1 and S1E25 language on purpose, so learners can feel how far they've come

chapters.a_plot: The Festa dei Tigli in the saved park, one long table down the street. Ben's speech, eloquent now, echoes his broken S1 toast. Emma announces her results: 100.
chapters.b_plot: Ornella's farewell toast, and Franco's reply. The last confessionale is Ben's: 'Mi chiamo Ben. Sono di Borgoverde.'
